methodology: Stored exact URLs/ALT from 61-post snapshot; canonical Commons file catalog text; independent LAC blog and University of Ottawa identifier for 1850 reward; remote CloudFront source rendered via web image viewer. This is NOT logged-out browser evidence, a complete license review or a binary-original check.

rows.stored_alt: Illustrated London News engraving of HMS Erebus and HMS Terror departing for the Arctic expedition in May 1845.
rows.institution: The Illustrated London News; Wikimedia Commons canonical file
rows.rights_evidence: Commons marks 1845 press illustration PD-old and PD-US; underlying source credited to Illustrated London News; publication/licensing must still be checked before localization.
rows.credit_candidate: Illustrated London News, May 24, 1845 / Wikimedia Commons
rows.review_note: This is a historical engraving, not a photograph; alt naming both ships is drawn from the print title.

rows.stored_alt: John Rae seated beside Franklin expedition relics, a Royal Geographical Society medal and a map in an 1886 portrait.
rows.institution: University of Washington Libraries Portraits Collection (via Commons)
rows.rights_evidence: Commons claims U.S. public domain for pre-1931 photograph; collection metadata explicitly warns dates/locations can be incorrect; primary UW catalog/item reuse restrictions unresolved.
rows.credit_candidate: Byrne and Co. / University of Washington Libraries Special Collections, Portraits Collection 2459
rows.review_note: Original is only 399px wide; never upscale to 960. Validate catalog against UW before permanent hosting.

rows.stored_alt: 1860 map showing the probable route of Erebus and Terror and areas searched after the Franklin expedition disappeared.
rows.rights_evidence: Commons PD-old/PDM and British Library out-of-copyright book account; colors/contrast of digital scan were automatically enhanced and not guaranteed historically authentic; verify item terms.
rows.credit_candidate: British Library, The North-West Passage (1860), HMNTS 10460.d.5 / Wikimedia Commons
rows.review_note: This is an 1860 retrospective map, not an eyewitness 1845 navigation chart.

rows.stored_alt: James Fitzjames photographed in 1845 shortly before sailing aboard HMS Erebus on the Franklin expedition.
rows.institution: Digital photographer FabTet on Wikimedia Commons
rows.rights_evidence: Modern digital photograph is released by its 2023 photographer under CC BY-SA 4.0; nineteenth-century daguerreotype antiquity does NOT erase modern photography's Commons license/attribution obligations.
rows.credit_candidate: FabTet, photograph of James Fitzjames daguerreotype, CC BY-SA 4.0; link author/license and mark adaptations
rows.review_note: Do not label this specific digital file generically public domain. Review attribution, license link, modification indications and share-alike implications before caching.

rows.stored_alt: British Admiralty poster from 1850 offering rewards for rescuing Franklin’s crews or determining their fate.
rows.institution: Library and Archives Canada; University of Ottawa corroboration
rows.rights_evidence: Commons copy claims public domain for 1850 reward broadside; LAC is identified as custodian by its own blog and University of Ottawa MIKAN record. Review primary item rights; government archive custody does not itself confer a license.
rows.credit_candidate: British Admiralty, W. A. B. Hamilton (1850), Library and Archives Canada e010754422 / MIKAN 2981240
rows.review_note: Current CloudFront file visibly showed the March 7 1850 £20,000 poster and LAC credit in independent image viewer. Proposed exact-document Commons archival candidate 726×1119; no binary/hash match yet.
